text.text_excerpt: Conundrum. Do I keep it my little secret, or spread the word? Last night my husband and I dined here after I did a search in Yelp. First, take a look at the menu outside. Second, head to the bar for a flight or glass of wine. Then head to the tiny kitchen window out back. Now...order one of anything that strikes your fancy. The food is amazing. Everything is house made, and, made to order. The chef told me they run out of pasta every evening. We had a Caesar salad, spicy meatballs, fettuccine with pomodoro sauce and Italian sausage, fusilli with fungi sauce, creamy with shallots, shrooms and sherry. Great little place in the back courtyard of The Tasting Room - different owners but quite a symbiotic relationship so hopefully we won't see constant restaurant change like other places in town such as Chickie Wah Wah. Meatballs were good as were a couple different pastas and sauces, and everything is seasoned well. On a second visit we once again had the shrimp piccata but this time tried the spicy tomato cream sauce and meatballs on rigatoni. The prices can seem a bit high for a little takeout window at maybe $9-14 per dish (once you add up all the components which are ordered a la carte) but this is excellent pasta that you'd be happy paying $20 for at a sit-down restaurant. Pasta is one of my favorite comfort foods and I have officially found my match. They hand make their pasta every day. Something that many restaurants have let go by the wayside. You design your own meal so, you start by picking your pasta, then your sauce, and then you can add any extras like sausage or shrimp. I went with a spicy red cream sauce. The sauce was full of flavor and had jalepenos so they weren't kidding when they said spicy. It was just the right amount of heat and the little bit of cream cut the acidity of the tomatoes. The pasta had perfect consistency and absorbed the flavors of the sauce. Simple, whole ingredients executed perfectly. That's amore.
